notes: Modified cash basis for governmental funds; proprietary funds are on the accrual basis (depreciation, receivables) and the Statement of Activities business-type column ties to the proprietary statement (net position 2,838,696 -> 2,811,897), so business-type lines come from the proprietary statement (p6) by cost type and business_type uses net position. Governmental lines from the Total Governmental Funds column (p4); fund balance rolls forward exactly (2,131,684 -> 2,079,009). Cash and investments are printed separately on the governmental funds statement of assets (p3, 2023 and 2022 comparative Total columns) and recorded as cash/investments; the cash figures do not roll forward on their own (the fund balances also include interfund receivables/payables and amounts due from other governments). 'Sales and miscellaneous taxes' 236,220 = Statement of Activities Sales taxes 236,220 (p2), so sales tax. Capital outlay 207,232 is entirely in the Auditorium Fund column, labelled Capital Outlay: Culture/Recreation. Utility 'Other operating revenues' 29,220 is counted in Charges for Services on the Statement of Activities, so charges for services/fees. Business-type receipts total = operating 454,790 + interest 717 (no single printed total); disbursements 592,226 as printed on the Statement of Activities (p2) = operating 591,651 + interest 575. Proprietary cash flows from the Total Proprietary Funds column (p7). Balance sheet: government-wide Statement of Net Position (p1); the governmental funds statement includes due to/from other funds 406,353 so its totals do not equal the government-wide figures.
